# Repository instructions

- This is a learning repository for an experienced Quality Engineer preparing for JavaScript/TypeScript automation work.
- Prefer focused, readable examples over broad application architecture or premature abstractions.
- Use synthetic test data only. Never add credentials, tokens, customer data, or proprietary material.
- Keep core helpers deterministic and side-effect free unless a lesson explicitly practices I/O.
- Add or update tests when changing behavior. Cover ordinary, boundary, and invalid inputs where relevant.
- Await asynchronous operations and preserve meaningful error context; do not swallow failures.
- TypeScript types document/check code at compile time; validate untrusted runtime data explicitly.
- Use descriptive names and comments to explain why, not to narrate obvious syntax.
- Keep generated output such as `dist/` out of Git. Before committing, review `git status` and the staged diff.
- Follow the lesson instructions and explain any trade-off in the pull request; do not replace exercises with opaque code.
